03The investment

Luxury hotels are investing heavily in wellness. But guests who’ve crossed time zones are often too exhausted from travelling to enjoy it, and don’t know what to use, and when, to feel better.

Why it stays that way

Wellness usually sits with a director responsible for the department’s operational and financial direction: the team, the standards, the budget.

Timing it to each guest’s journey means connecting the rooms, the food, the spa and the gym, which sit across different departments, so currently no one owns it across the hotel.

That’s what ALT‑15° does, using AI and circadian rhythm science, personalised and bespoke to each guest.

06The commercial case

When every luxury hotel can buy the same wellness inventory, owning it stops being a reason to choose you.

For a guest who’s crossed time zones, wellness means recovery.

Today: amenities to list
  • Spa and treatments
  • Gym and recovery suite
  • Sleep and room environment
  • Restaurants and room service
And decisions to make

What to eat, which treatment and whether there’s time for one, what exercise to do and whether to visit the gym at all. Every choice is left to a guest already emotionally drained and low on energy from the journey, with jet lag compounding both.

77% of long-haul travellers say jet lag affects their concentration.*

→
With Travel Performance: an offer to sell

We time light, food, movement, sleep and treatments to each guest’s journey, so every service your hotel already offers works with their circadian rhythm, not against it.

These are departments you already run, and once they’re timed to the guest, they become reasons to book, spend and return.

Decisions eliminated

Before they arrive, each guest receives a recommended plan for the whole stay, timed to their body clock: when to eat, when to train, when to recover and when to sleep. Every service is offered at the right time for them, so there’s nothing left to decide or figure out. That peace of mind has a price, and it’s yours to sell.

10What the hotel already knows

The flight number isn’t just data. It’s the start of the guest experience.

Whether a guest has crossed one time zone or eight, most hotels look
after them in exactly the same way.

01  Already in the booking
  • Where they’ve come from
  • How many time zones they’ve crossed
  • How long they’ve been travelling
  • What time it is for their body on arrival
02  A short questionnaire before arrival

Sent with the booking confirmation: whether they’re a morning or evening person and the purpose of the trip.

03  A bespoke plan for each guest

Emailed before arrival: when to eat, train, recover and sleep across the stay.
They can accept or change any part of it, and the hotel has everything arranged and ready for when they arrive.

11The returning guest

Most hotels forget a guest at checkout. Yours keeps learning about them.

Stay 1

The hotel learns

From a business traveller’s booking and questionnaire data, the hotel sets his plan: when and what he eats, how, where and for how long he trains, and when he recovers and sleeps, set by the time zones he’s crossed and the schedule ahead of him. His body clock, and which parts of the plan he accepted, changed or declined, start his travel profile,* alongside his other preferences.

After he leaves

The hotel stays with him

After checkout, the usual last contact is the bill and a review request. Yours follows him home: where he’s opted in, your email or app sends his recovery plan for the days after the flight, when to sleep, train and eat. Each message carries your brand into his routine, keeping the hotel front of mind until he books again.

Stay 2 onwards

The hotel optimises every stay

How he recovers is added to his travel profile, so when he books again it already holds his body clock and what he accepted, changed or declined last time. The new journey, and anything that’s changed, is added, so his plan builds on everything the hotel already knows about him. At any other hotel, he’d be starting again with a team that knows nothing about how he travels.

*Designed to carry preferences from one stay to the next, where your systems and guest permissions allow.

13The results

Six months later. Six improvements in your hotel.

01  Your guests

Faster recovery

Designed to reduce guests’ jet lag recovery time, so they sleep well, think clearly and are physically ready sooner. They’re at their best for the meetings, events or occasions they travelled for, and go home without losing days to recovery.

02  Your teams

One plan, every department

Every department works from the same plan for each guest, so they know what to offer and when, without having to learn circadian science. Your team still leads the hospitality, without disruption.

03  Your sales and marketing

A stay worth paying more for

A package priced above the standard room rate, and a story to sell to international travellers and corporate clients, who are buying back the days travel usually costs them.

04  Your facilities

Busier at quieter hours

Each guest’s plan follows their body clock, not the clock on the wall, so demand spreads across the day. Spa, gym and restaurants are used more, including during off-peak hours, increasing the return on the facilities you’ve already invested in.

05  Your brand

Your brand goes home with them

Branded recovery plans follow guests home, keeping your hotel front of mind until they book again.

06  Your position

A reason to choose you
